props.classMechanic_text:
MONK MECHANIC — SOUL BEADS

“Steady breath, steady light.”

What Are Soul Beads?

Soul Beads are motes of disciplined spirit. They appear as charms, floating orbs, glowing marks—how do yours manifest? You manage two states: Core Soul Beads (your starting set) and Resolve Soul Beads (generated over time once you start releasing Core).

  • Limit: equals half your Willpower die size (min 3, max 6).
  • Start of conflict: You begin with a full set of Core Soul Beads. Core does not count for the Clarity Skill.
  • After you start releasing Core: you gain 2 Resolve Soul Beads per turn, up to your Soul Bead limit.

Your Soul Bead Limit (Examples)

Willpower DieHalfSoul Bead LimitNotes
d633Minimum floor is 3
d844—
d1055—
d1266Maximum cap is 6

How the Engine Runs

  1. Start full: You enter with Core Beads = your limit.
  2. Spend Core with Monk skills (heal, attack, defend). The moment you first release Core, your Resolve flow begins.
  3. Generate Resolve: At the end of each of your turns, gain +2 Resolve Beads (up to your limit). These do count for Clarity.
  4. Maintain or spend: Resolve Beads power your toolkit and also fuel Clarity’s passive bonuses (by pairs). Balance “banking for buffs” vs “spending for effects.”

Clarity & Resonance (Core Skills)

Clarity (SL +3)

  • For each pair of active Resolve Beads you possess, choose one benefit:
  • • Immunity to a chosen status.
  • • Your attacks/spells of a chosen damage type ignore Resistances.
  • • Resistance to a chosen damage type.
  • You can maintain up to [SL] benefits at once, and you can’t pick the same benefit more than once.

Resonant Clarity (SL +3)

Your clarity radiates outward. For each [SL], you may share one of your active Clarity benefits with allies, up to three creatures.

Active Skills — Spend Beads with Purpose

Soul Renewal

Action. Choose up to three creatures. Release Beads toward them, spending 2 MP per Bead. Each delivered Bead restores 10 HP or MP (your choice). Improves at L20 → 12, L40 → 15 per Bead. Each Bead released is destroyed.

Spirit Shot (SL +2)

Action. Choose any number of Beads. Spend 2 MP per Bead, then make a [DEX + WLP] Check. On a hit, each target loses [SL × 4] HP or MP per Bead (you choose), ignoring Resistances. HP shots test Defense; MP shots test Magical Defense. Beads are destroyed whether you hit or not.

Spiritual Fortress (SL +3)

Reaction. Release any number of Beads to reduce incoming damage to you or up to three creatures by [SL × 2] per Bead, before applying Affinities. Each Bead destroyed this way costs 2 MP.

Heroic Skills — When your practice becomes legend

Crystal Clear

  • Requires Clarity (SL 3).
  • With a full set of Resolve Beads, you gain +2 to Defense, Magical Defense, and Accuracy Checks.
  • With Resonant Clarity, allies gain +1 to those stats from you.

Beaded Weapon

  • If you have a full set of Soul Beads, spend 40 MP to imbue one equipped weapon.
  • Weapon gains +3 Accuracy and its damage ignores Resistances.
  • If melee, it also becomes ranged (can be launched from afar).
  • If the weapon is equipped while casting, make a free attack as part of the same action.
  • You lose access to the Beads used; they don’t count toward Clarity while imbued. You can generate new Beads from next turn.
  • Only one weapon can be imbued at a time.

Turn Flow — Step by Step

  1. Opening State: Core Beads = limit. Pick no Clarity yet (Core doesn’t count).
  2. First Release: Spend any number of Core with Renewal / Shot / Fortress / other effects.
  3. End of Turn: Begin the Resolve flow: gain +2 Resolve (bank up to your limit).
  4. Clarity Online: For every pair of active Resolve, choose a benefit (up to [SL] simultaneous). Swap choices as Bead counts change on your turns.
  5. Repeat: Each turn, decide between conserving Resolve to keep Clarity stacks vs. spending for effects.

Table tip: Track Core and Resolve separately (two rows of tokens). Flip or move tokens to a “spent” box when destroyed.

Worked Examples

Example A — Bring Clarity Online, then Share: You start with 5 Core (limit 5). Turn 1, you don’t spend—instead you release 1 Core with a minor Soul Renewal (healing 10), starting the flow. End of Turn 1 → you gain +2 Resolve (now 2 Resolve active). Turn 2: pick Clarity benefit #1 (e.g., Resistance to Fire). End of Turn 2 → +2 Resolve (now 4 active) → pick benefit #2 (e.g., Immunity: Poisoned). With Resonant Clarity at sufficient SL, you share those benefits to allies (up to 3 targets).

Example B — Spirit Shot Burst (SL 2): You choose to spend 3 Beads on Spirit Shot and pay 6 MP. Roll [DEX+WLP]; on a hit, each enemy in the attack loses 3 × ([SL × 4]) = 3 × 8 = 24 HP (or MP) ignoring Resistances. Whether you hit or miss, those 3 Beads are destroyed, so your Clarity stacks may drop—plan for that.

Example C — Spiritual Fortress as Panic Button (SL 3): A big AoE is coming. As a reaction, you release 2 Beads to reduce damage by 2 × ([SL × 2]) = 2 × 6 = 12 to you and up to two allies (or up to three creatures total), paying 4 MP. Damage reductions apply before Affinities.

Pocket Card (Hand to Players)

  1. Start: Core = limit. Core doesn’t count for Clarity.
  2. First Release: Spend any Core → begin flow.
  3. Each End of Turn: +2 Resolve (cap = limit).
  4. Clarity: Every 2 Resolve = pick a benefit; max [SL] benefits active; no duplicates.
  5. Spend: Renewal (heal 10/12/15), Shot (2 MP/Bead, [DEX+WLP], [SL×4] per Bead, ignores Resist.), Fortress (reaction, [SL×2] reduce per Bead, 2 MP/Bead).
  6. Heroic: Crystal Clear (+2 self, +1 allies via Resonance with full Resolve set), Beaded Weapon (40 MP, +3 Acc, ignore Resist., may become ranged; you lose those Beads while imbued).

props.class_lore: Monks are masters of mind, body, and spirit, using their inner clarity to achieve supernatural feats. Through rigorous discipline, they can harness raw spiritual might to endure adversity, aid their allies, and strike with precision. Monks seek to maintain balance — within themselves and in the world around them — believing that true strength lies not in mastering combat, but in understanding the nature of conflict itself. Some monks choose solitude to perfect their discipline, while others act as conduits to harmonious living, helping the world around them
